FOREWORD
0.3 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been taken from Advisory Circular No. 150/5345-10 E ( 1984 ) issued by the Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration, USA. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised J.

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 24 November 1987, after the draft finalized by the Illuminating Engineering and Luminaires Sectional Commlttee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 Airport ground lighting systems are operated on a constant current ( 6'6 A or 20 A ) &pply fed from a constant current regulator. The regulator capacity should be adequate to provide for load and power loss in series circuit. Different types of constant current regulators are used employing resonant circuit, transducers, thyristors, etc. This standard covers requirements of all types of constant current regulators using the above principles in both higher and lower ratings.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This specification covers the requirements for constant current regulators for use in airport series lighting circuits. 2. CLASSIFICATION 2.1 The various types of constant current regulators covered by this standard have been classified in Table 1.

3.1.3 Altitude - Any altitude from sea level to 3 050 m above sea level. 4. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Input Voltage - Input voltage shall be specified by the purchaser with a tolerance limit of + 10 and -5 percent. Regulators of 10, 15, and 20 kW may comply with the above criteria. As an alternative, resonant-type regulators smaller than 10 kW may be supplied with taps for 250, 240, 230, 220 and 208 V from which the proper tap may be selected for various supply voltages. The regulators shall be designed to withstand momentary increases of voltages up to 120 percent of the nominal input voltage without being shut off or damaged by such overvoltage. The duration of such overvoltage excursions shall be not longer than 50 milliseconds and shall occur no more than once in a 1 minute interval. External control power may be utilized if desired. 4.2 Circuit Isdation - The power input circuit shall be electrically isolated from the output circuit. The peak output voltage of an opencircuited regulator shall not exceed two times the rated wattage divided by the rated current or 4 250 V peak, whichever is greater. These measurements shall be made with an oscilloscope or high voltage peak reading meter. 1

7.1.2.1 The sampling procedure and criteria of acceptance shall be subject to agreement between the supplier and the purchaser. 7.1.3 Routine Tests - The following shall constitute routine tests and shall be carried out. on each regulator: a) Visual examination ( see 7.2 ), b) Remote control test ( see 7.4 ), c) Dielectric tests ( see 7.10 ), d) Protective device tests ( see 7.11 ), and e) Leakage test ( see 7.13 ). 7.2 Visual Examination - Regulator shall not have any visible sign of damage. Compliance is checked by visual examination. 7.3 Regulation - The following tests shall be performed to demonstrate compliance with the requirements specified in 5.1 and Table 2. Where isolating transformers and lamps are not specifically required, a resistive load may be used. 7.3.1 Input Vohage Tests - For regulators 10 kW and larger, the regulator should be loaded to full load and energized with nominal input voltage, 110 percent of nominal voltage, and 90 percent of nominal voltage and the output current should be verified to see if it falls within the limits of Table 2. This test is repeated at half load and short circuit. These tests shall be repeated at all brightness settings. For resonant regulators under 10 kW, the regulator is energized with 250, 240, 230, 220 and 208 V and the output current is verified to see if it falls within the limits of Table 2. This test shall be conducted at short circuit, half load, and full load and at all brightness settings. Non-resonant regulators under 10 kW may meet either criteria. 7.3.2 Inductive Load Tests - For regulators 10 kW and larger, an equivalent of full load and half load shall be placed on the regulator, but with 30 percent of the isolating transformers open-circuited. The input voltages shall be nominal, 110 percent of nominal, and ~95percent of nominal voltage. The output current shall be checked at all brightness settings and shall be within the limits of Table 2. For regulators under 10 kW, the regulator shall be energized with 240 V and an equivalent of full load and half load on the secondary at the 100 percent brightness step. The secondaries of 30 percent of isolating transformers shall be openthe circuited, and the output current shall not rise above 6'8 amperes. 7.4 Remote Control Test - Check the output current at all brightness steps using the following remote control circuits ( a resistance load may be used in lieu of the full length specified ) and

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products arc also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a Details of conditions under which further safeguard. a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

7.6 Efficiency - With nominal input voltage and a full load of unity power factor, the efficiency at maximum brightness shall not be less than that specified in Table 3. 7.7 Power Factor - With nominal input voltage and a full load of unity power factor, the power factor at maximum brightness shall be not less than that specified in 5.3. 7.8 High Temperature - Place the regulator in a test chamber and maintain the ambient temperature at 55 f 2�C. After the temperature of the regulator components has stabilized, operate the regulator for 4 hours at full rated input and output values. Perform the tests in 7.3.1 to demonstrate high temperature operation. 7.9 Low Temperature - Place the regulator in a test chamber and maintain the ambient temperature at -40 f 2�C for 12 hours. Perform the tests in 7.3.1 while maintaining a temperature of -40�C to demonstrate low temperature operation ( remote control may be used ).

7.12 Transient Suppression - To demonstrate the effectiveness of lightning arrestors, they shall suppress a test pulse on the output lines consisting of a 10 to 20 microsecond current surge of 15 000 amperes with the subsequent powerfollow current and a voltage surge of 10 kW per microsecond, Min without damage to the regulator. 7.13 Leakage Test - Test each oil-filled regulator assembly to determine that all welds and gasketed seals are tight. Utilize an internal air pressure of 690 =t 50 Nm' for 5 minutes. 7.14 Output Current Surge Test - The output of the regulator shall be checked to determine compliance with 4.13.
